titleEn: Centuries before TikTok, this 1579 bestseller gave readers their daily dose of ‘brain rot’
titleZh: TikTok 之前的“脑腐”读物：1579 年畅销书中的碎片化消遣
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: First you are shown a new hack to keep wine from spoiling. Then a dog lovingly devoted to its owner. Immediately in tow there are methods to repair broken glass and remove acne, a tip for weight loss, a cake recipe and an astrological reading of your future. But this is not your TikTok or Instagram feed – it’s the contents of a book written nearly four-and-a-half centuries ago.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，你会看到一种防止葡萄酒变质的新方法。然后是一只对主人充满爱意的狗。紧接着是修复碎玻璃和去除粉刺的方法、减肥秘诀、蛋糕食谱和对你未来的占星阅读。但这不是你的TikTok或Instagram--这是一本写于近450年前的书的内容。

paragraphs.en: The English writer Thomas Lupton’s book A Thousand Notable Things was first published in 1579. True to its title, it collected roughly 1,000 short passages ordered randomly, one after another. A seemingly endless stream of household “life hacks”, sensational stories and recipes, it offered answers for just about everything.
paragraphs.zh: 英国作家托马斯卢普顿的《一千件值得注意的事》一书于1579年首次出版。正如书名所言，这本书收集了大约1,000段随机排列的短文。这本书似乎源源不断地讲述了家庭生活中的“窍门”、耸人听闻的故事和食谱，为几乎所有的事情提供了答案。

paragraphs.en: Trouble sleeping? Rub your forehead with a mix of white poppy and henbane seeds. If you find yourself bewitched, leave a mercury-filled quill under your pillow. And have you heard the folklore that claims when a robin red breast finds a dead human, they cover its face in moss?
paragraphs.zh: 睡不着吗用白色罂粟和天仙子的混合种子擦额头。如果你发现自己被施了魔法，在枕头下放一支水银羽毛笔。你听说过民间传说吗？当知更鸟的红色乳房发现一个死人时，它们会用苔藓覆盖它的脸。

paragraphs.en: Flitting through eclectic, attention-grabbing short-form content may be the de facto mode of media consumption in the 21st century. But how-to books like A Thousand Notable Things suggest that our ancestors’ preoccupations were not entirely different.
paragraphs.zh: 浏览兼收并蓄、引人注目的简短内容可能是21世纪世纪媒体消费的实际模式。但《一千件值得注意的事》这样的指导性书籍表明，我们祖先的关注点并没有完全不同。

paragraphs.en: Lupton understood the wide appeal of such easily digestible material. In a revealing preface, he argued that imbibing many passages of “strangeness and variety” was preferable to being “fed too long with one food” by reading entire books.
paragraphs.zh: 卢普顿明白这种容易消化的材料的广泛吸引力，他在一个发人深省的序言中指出，吸收许多“陌生和多样”的段落比阅读整本书“长时间吃一种食物”更好。

paragraphs.en: It proved a winning formula. A Thousand Notable Things enjoyed at least 33 editions, remaining in print from the time Sir Francis Drake was circumnavigating the globe until 1827, the year the first known photograph was taken.
paragraphs.zh: 事实证明，这是一个成功的公式。《一千件值得注意的事情》至少有33个版本，从弗朗西斯德雷克爵士环游地球仪到1827年，也就是第一张已知照片拍摄的那一年，这本书一直在印刷。

paragraphs.en: Its success belonged to a burgeoning taste for “books of secrets”, recipe-like instructional texts that taught everything from cosmetics and alchemy to brewing and beekeeping.
paragraphs.zh: 它的成功归功于对“秘密之书”的新兴品味，这是一种类似食谱的教学文本，教授从化妆品和炼金术到酿造和养蜂的一切。

paragraphs.en: Originating in Italy, and published throughout the 16th, 17th and 18th centuries, the most popular of these works were continually translated and reprinted throughout Europe. They are now recognised as exerting genuine influence on contemporary scientific culture.
paragraphs.zh: 这些著作起源于意大利，在16、17和18世纪出版，其中最受欢迎的作品在整个欧洲不断被翻译和重印，现在被认为对当代科学文化产生了真正的影响。

paragraphs.en: Whether providing alchemical routes to the philosopher’s stone or the recipe for a nutritious stew, books like A Thousand Notable Things thrived on the promise of revealing hidden “secrets” about nature’s inner workings.
paragraphs.zh: 无论是提供通往点金石的炼金术路线，还是提供营养丰富的炖菜配方，像《一千件值得注意的事情》这样的书都因其揭示大自然内部运作的隐藏“秘密”的承诺而蓬勃发展。

paragraphs.en: Of course, there was no guarantee that everything Lupton suggested would work: whether sleeping on your right side during pregnancy really meant the baby would be female, or that dreaming of eagles flying overhead was necessarily a sign of imminent good fortune. Sheer efficacy alone wasn’t the point. The appeal lay in the wonder, curiosity and amusement that accompanied practical instruction.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，不能保证卢普顿建议的一切都能奏效：怀孕时朝右侧睡是否真的意味着孩子是女的，或者梦见老鹰在头顶飞过是否一定是即将到来的好运的征兆。纯粹的功效并不是重点。吸引人的是伴随着实用指导的惊奇、好奇和娱乐。

paragraphs.en: If some passages sound absurd or downright dangerous to modern ears (henbane and mercury are highly poisonous), consider that much of Lupton’s material was cutting-edge in its day. His most cited source was Antoine Mizauld, a Parisian medical professor and advisor to French queen Marguerite de Valois.
paragraphs.zh: 如果有些段落在现代人听来荒谬或危险（天仙子和水银都是剧毒），那就想想卢普顿的许多材料在当时都是最前沿的。他最常被引用的资料来源是安托万·米佐德（Antoine Mizauld），他是巴黎医学教授，也是法国王后玛格丽特·德·瓦卢瓦（Marguerite de Valois）的顾问。

paragraphs.en: Even though the vitality of astrology, occult science and ancient medicine waned over the book’s 250-year lifespan, the deeply human concerns it addressed proved enduringly popular.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管占星术、神秘科学和古代医学的生命力在这本书的250年寿命中逐渐减弱，但它所解决的人类深层问题却广受欢迎。

paragraphs.en: Personal copies
paragraphs.zh: 个人副本

paragraphs.en: We know that contemporary readers found Lupton’s eclectic material engaging thanks to their annotations in personal copies, precious few of which remain today.
paragraphs.zh: 我们知道，当代读者发现卢普顿的折衷材料从事感谢他们的注释在个人副本，其中珍贵的几个今天仍然存在。

paragraphs.en: One survivor from 1612, now in the Glasgow University Library, is marked with small crosses at passages on lameness, heart trouble, ulcers, meat eating and stomach problems. We might speculate that its owner was managing symptoms of dietary issues or gout. So too are gout cures underlined in a copy owned by the 17th-century book collector Frances Wolfreston.
paragraphs.zh: 一本1612年的幸存者，现藏于格拉斯哥大学图书馆（University Library），书中的段落上用小十字标记着跛足、心脏病、溃疡、吃肉和胃病。我们可以推测，它的主人当时正在控制饮食问题或痛风的症状。17世纪图书收藏家弗朗西斯·沃尔弗雷斯顿（Frances Wolfreston）拥有的一本书中，痛风的治疗方法也是如此。

paragraphs.en: Another reader pencilled crosses next to 38 predominantly medical passages in their 1706 copy, including remedies for head and toothaches, burning eyes, shortness of breath, sore throat and insomnia.
paragraphs.zh: 另一位读者在1706年的版本中，在38个主要是医学的段落旁边画了十字，包括头痛和牙痛、眼睛灼热、呼吸急促、喉咙痛和失眠的治疗方法。

paragraphs.en: Others were more selective. One copy in the Wellcome Collection is marked only occasionally, including at an anecdote about a German farmer who died with terrible pain in his side. A surgeon cut him open to find large pieces of wood and four steel knives, afflictions that were blamed on the Devil.
paragraphs.zh: 其他的则更有选择性。《维康收藏集》中有一本书只是偶尔被标记，包括一个关于一个德国农民的轶事，他死的时候身体两侧疼痛难忍。一位外科医生把他切开，发现了大块木头和四把钢刀，这些痛苦被归咎于魔鬼。

paragraphs.en: Just as we worry today about the pernicious effects of TikTok, 16th-century commentators also feared the “brain-rotting” potential of low-brow mass entertainment, distraction and information overload.
paragraphs.zh: 就像我们今天担心TikTok的有害影响一样，16世纪的评论家也担心低俗的大众娱乐、分心和信息过载的“大脑腐烂”潜力。

paragraphs.en: But Lupton’s take was more optimistic. Offering bite-size morsels gleaned from a wide range of texts, in plain English rather than scholarly Latin, gave ordinary readers access to knowledge that otherwise required whole libraries to attain.
paragraphs.zh: 但卢普顿的看法更为乐观，他认为，用简明的英语而不是学术性的拉丁语，提供从广泛文本中收集到的一口大小的信息，让普通读者能够接触到知识，而这些知识需要整个图书馆才能获得。

paragraphs.en: These how to books, which are the subject of an ongoing research collaboration between Glasgow University and the Herzog August library in Germany, will take centre stage in an exhibition at the Mitchell Library, Glasgow, from January to March 2027.
paragraphs.zh: 这些书籍是格拉斯哥大学和德国赫尔佐格·奥古斯特图书馆正在进行的研究合作的主题，将于2027年1月至3月在格拉斯哥米切尔图书馆举行的展览中占据中心地位。

paragraphs.en: Whether or not they are direct antecedents of today’s instructional media, these texts encapsulate both the past’s profound strangeness, and those facets of human experience that seem perennial: the potent dialectic of similarity and difference that makes history so compelling. If nothing else, they might provide a handy hack to stave off your next headache.
paragraphs.zh: 无论它们是否是当今教学媒体的直接前身，这些文本都概括了过去深刻的陌生感，以及人类经验中似乎永恒的那些方面：相似性和差异性的强有力辩证法，使历史如此引人注目。如果没有别的，它们可能会提供一个方便的黑客来避免你的下一个头痛。
